title: Polymer clay faux blue goldstone pendant
subtitle: Deep blue metallic-fleck pendant imitating goldstone glass
excerpt: Blue goldstone's glittering metallic effect comes from metallic inclusions in glass. In polymer clay, the same effect is created by mixing deep blue clay with fine gold or copper mica powder and tiny fragments of metallic leaf, then rolling and shaping a pendant. No kiln is required.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Faux-stone polymer clay methods are a widely documented craft technique.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling material that hardens in a domestic oven at 110 to 130°C
Fine metallic mineral pigment powder used to add shimmer or metallic effects to polymer clay

content.text: Goldstone is a type of glass with copper or chromium inclusions that catch the light in a dark glittering pattern. In
polymer clay
, mixing deep navy clay with
mica powder
and tiny fragments of gold or copper metallic leaf creates the same glittering depth. No kiln is required: the pendant hardens in a domestic oven.

materials.name: Gold metallic transfer leaf (a small fragment)

tools.name: Pottery rolling pin or acrylic roller

content.text: Mixing the goldstone clay
Condition the navy clay until smooth and pliable. Flatten it into a disc in the palm.

Sprinkle mica powder over the surface of the disc. Fold the disc and press the powder inside. Roll and fold several times until the mica is evenly distributed through the clay body. Do not overwork or the metallic flecks will blur into a uniform sheen rather than keeping their sparkle effect.
Optional: tear very small irregular fragments of metallic leaf and fold them into the clay at this stage. These create larger, more irregular light-catching spots alongside the fine mica.
Forming the pendant
Roll the mixed clay into a slab about 6 mm thick. Cut a rounded rectangle or teardrop shape about 3.5 cm by 2.5 cm.
Smooth the edges by rolling them lightly between two fingers. Pierce a hanging hole at the top with the needle tool.
Buff the face of the pendant with a clean fingertip in small circular strokes to bring out the mica shimmer. The mica particles align under the pressure and catch light more strongly.
Curing
Place on a ceramic tile and cure at 130°C for 25 minutes. Ventilate the kitchen. Do not use the same tray for food cookware.
Finishing
Sand through 400 then 800 grit under water to remove the matte cured surface and reveal the metallic depth. Buff to a high gloss with a soft cloth. Thread a bail through the hanging hole.
Use and care
Decorative pendant; not food-safe. Wipe with a dry cloth. Avoid prolonged contact with water and solvents.
Variations
Use red-brown clay with gold mica for a red goldstone look. Use black clay with silver mica for a charcoal glittering effect.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Mica has blurred into a uniform sheen rather than individual sparkle
items.cause: Clay was overworked after the mica was added
items.fix: Mix mica for fewer folds next time. A slight variation in concentration creates more natural depth. The blurred version still looks good sanded and buffed

items.problem: Pendant cracks on the edges after curing
items.cause: Clay was not conditioned enough before shaping, leaving micro-stress in the edges
items.fix: Condition more thoroughly at the start. Edge cracks can be filled with a small amount of raw clay pressed in and re-cured for 10 minutes
